note: Generic per-type strategy prose written for the final60 design. No text from any existing proof; Lean snippets are at most 39 characters and always in backticks.

short-tactic: Short proof: first test a one-line candidate that closes the whole goal with a single closer such as `simp_all`, `grind`, `omega`, `norm_num`, `positivity` or `decide`; if one compiles it usually dominates both ratios.
Look for a term-mode or one-lemma answer: an existing lemma applied to the hypotheses, or `exact` with anonymous constructors, is usually shorter and cheaper than a tactic script.
Merge adjacent `rw` and `simp only` calls, drop `show` lines and one-use `have` steps, and keep only the simp lemmas that are needed; compare bare `simp` with `simp only` by the combined score.
structural-induction: Induction or case proof: do the split once and close the branches together, for example `induction h <;> simp_all` or `cases h <;> grind`, then repair only the branches that still fail.
Reuse the congruence, inversion and preservation lemmas stated before this theorem in the source context instead of re-deriving them in each branch; search the corpus by the relation's name.
If the statement applies a recursive function to the induction variable, try `fun_induction` or the definition's own induction principle, and generalize only what a branch needs.
Bullets with identical bodies can share one `<;>` or `all_goals`; one-use `have` and `obtain` steps can be inlined, and `show` lines and type ascriptions dropped.
algebra-analysis-long: Long algebraic proof: most of its length usually re-derives facts the library already has; replace `have` chains by one lemma, or by `field_simp` then `ring`, `linear_combination`, `nlinarith`, `positivity` or `gcongr`.
The largest measured reductions came from a new short route through a library theorem rather than from local edits; spend an early candidate on such a route before polishing.
Factor repeated blocks: prove a shared argument once as a local `∀` claim and apply it, or close parallel goals with one combinator; drop `show` lines and one-use `have` steps.
To cut heartbeats, avoid whole-context `simp_all` or `aesop` on large goals and prefer targeted `rw`, `simp only [...]` and explicit lemma arguments.
competition: Competition proof: try a direct closer for each claim, for example `nlinarith [sq_nonneg (a - b)]`, `norm_num`, `omega`, `positivity`, `interval_cases` with `omega`, or `decide` on small finite cases.
Long competition proofs often re-prove standard facts; search for the key library lemma and collapse the surrounding `have` chain into a few steps.
Keep the answer and the witnesses exactly as stated; only the proof changes. Prefer fewer, stronger steps over many small `have` claims.

conditional.many_versions: This proof must compile unchanged on every listed version ({versions}); avoid recently added or renamed tactics, options and lemma names, and prefer core tactics and long-stable names.
conditional.hb_heavy: The original is expensive to elaborate (about {hb_millions} million raw heartbeats); removing broad automation, repeated normalisation or kernel computation can gain more than shortening.

header: Routing notes: generic strategy hypotheses chosen from static features of this problem; they are not verified edits and are never taken from any existing proof. Problem class: {problem_type}. Test each idea with a complete candidate.
